page.layout: One page of text in a single column, with a running head and page number at the top. Under the running head is a full-width summary paragraph in smaller type, then a decorative ornament strip (not transcribed), then a centred title "DE FULMINE." above the numbered paragraphs 3 to 7. The catchword sits at the right below the last line. No marginal notes.

main_text.l: 2. Meteora ignita, vel sunt magis insignia, ut fulmen, & Cometa; vel
minus insignia, ut fax, lancea, Draco volans &c. Nos autem primò agemus de
fulmine; secundò de Cometa, tertiò de reliquis meteoris igneis.
DE FULMINE.
3. Fulmen est meteorum ignitum ortum ex calida & sicca exhalatio-
ne, quæ cum vapore aqueo ad mediam aëris regionem delata,
ibique à vapore aut nube vehementer compressa, ac tandem accensa, nu-
bem effringit, & sic tonitru, fulgur, ac fulmen efficitur, adeo ut tonitru
sit sonus, fulgur sit splendor, & fulmen ipsa exhalatio magno impetu è
nube excussa.
4. Fulmen triplex est (scilicet terebrans, discutiens, & urens: Primum
est flammeum, & materiæ valde subtilis, & ideo in angustissimas rimulas
corporum se insinuat: Secundum est crassum ex materia valde compacta,
ideo corpora obvia disrumpit [?], illudque interdum lapis fulmineus comi-
tatur juxta communem Philosophorum sententiam: Tertium est magis
igneum quàm flammeum, ideo corpora objecta in ignem convertit.
5. Effectus fulminis præcipui sunt. Primò, fulmen interdum firmiora
& magis resistentia potentius ferit; minus autem resistentibus parcit; verbi
gratiâ liquefacit argentum illæsa crumena, gladium disrumpit intacta va-
gina, ossa diffringit incolumi carne: Tales autem effectus conveniunt ful-
mini terebranti ex partibus tenuissimis, sed actuosissimis composito, quod
parcit rebus mollibus, porosis, & rarefactis, quales sunt cutis, caro, cru-
mena, vagina, laurus &c. disrumpit verò dura & solida, qualia sunt ar-
gentum, ferrum, ossa &c.
6. Secundò, fulmen illæsa re solidiori fluidiorem consumit, ut cùm illæso

pter subtilitatem & tenuitatem transeunt per dolium porosum ipso illæso;
at propter calorem & siccitatem reducunt vinum in fumos subtiles, & sic
ipsum consumunt. Idem fulmen consumit substantiam cerebri humidi, il-
læsis partibus illis porosis capitis per quas transiit.
7. Tertiò, fulmen interdum totum dolium comburit, vino non effluen-
te; qui effectus convenit fulmini vrenti; cum enim tunc exhalatio in-

page.notes: Doubtful readings: in the summary line "vel minus" is partly obscured by a blurred band, read as "minus" [?] (not marked in text since the word is legible). "disrumpit" in paragraph 4 is printed with a long-s-like form, read as "disrumpit" [?]. "composito" in paragraph 5 is hard to make out, read as "composito". Top of the page is shaded by the scan. Catchword "lore" is the start of the next word "calore", split at the line end. Digitiser watermark at the foot is not transcribed. Spelling normalised as per rule 5: the running head and title are printed in capitals (SECVNDA, FVLMINE), given as SECUNDA and FULMINE; consonant v in conuertit, conuenit, obuia, euocatis, vehementer, vino, vrenti kept as v; "illæso" read from "illæfo".
